# TTD CI gate baseline (PLAN #40 Phase 0, Step 2, requirements BR-7 / BR-8 / BR-9).
# Read by core/tests/debugger/ttd/bench/ttdbench_test.cpp.
# Exported by tools/verification/ttd-bench/ttd_bench_compare.py from a run of
# engine controller, set ci, ttd-query-engine@cc1c7fb32, Release, MacStudio.localdomain.
# Deterministic metrics only (bytes, bytes and operations per frame): timings do not
# belong in a stored baseline.
# Columns: <configuration>/<workload> <metric> <value> <tolerance percent>
# Tolerance 0 = exact; heap metrics follow the allocator's growth policy.
# ATM3/idle rows updated 2026-10-31 (GMX phase 7, DS12887 periodic flag): the Ds12887 blob (id 18) carries the periodic divider position, 8 bytes more (state v3); the idle ROM sees the clock's PF, so RAM and compression rows moved slightly; the blob now changes every capture while a periodic rate runs (bm9 ds12887 rows).
# ATM3/idle rows updated 2026-11-14 (6de779c75, ZX-Evo ERS floppy boot): with no NVRAM file the machine starts with the EVO Reset Service defaults (virtual drive on D, CRC valid) instead of blank CMOS, so the idle ROM takes another path: RAM, compression, DS12887, ATM paging and Beta Disk rows moved.
# 48K/idle and PENTAGON/game bm7_file rows updated 2026-11-15 (Z80 Q latch per instruction class, qregister.h): the checkpoints carry the corrected Q, the compressed file moved by 3 / 5 bytes; no other row changed.
# bm7_file rows updated 2026-11-17 (F3, chunked streams): the header declares the chunked twins of the write journal and the holder streams (stream 0x8000 + S, "chunked-<name>"), 102 bytes more in every file; no other row changed.
# ATM3/idle, PENTAGON/idle and PENTAGON/game rows updated 2026-11-17 (card-positions, gs-debugger design §8): the NeoGS blob (id 12) carries the card CPU's instruction count, which advances every frame: the device-blob, bm3_ram_payload and NeoGS bm9 rows grow by ~6 bytes per frame, the file by ~5 (first NeoGS blob +13 / +14 bytes); no other row moved beyond its tolerance.
# 48K/idle, PENTAGON/idle and PENTAGON/game bm7_file rows updated 2026-11-19 (re-api-efficiency F2, split-independent RunNFrames): the bench runs one RunNFrames(1) per frame; each call used to drop the overshoot of its last instruction, so the live end drifted a few T-states per frame into the next frame, and the saved file's tail (the part of the frame after the last capture) was that much longer. Now every call ends a few T past the boundary: 1 / 4 / 18 bytes less; no other row changed.
# PENTAGON/game bm3_coverage_bpf and bm3_total_bpf updated 2026-11-22 (P1.S10 follow-up, coverage block summaries): the coverage index builds each block's summary as its frames seal (the keys united with their first and last frame, per-frame counts and written rows), so its open block holds that block's keys and a sparse bit set (a 512-byte leaf per 4 KB of key space reached): about 1.2 MB more over the 60 frames, which never seal a block; sealed summaries add about 180-225 bytes a frame in long sessions. No other row moved beyond its tolerance.
# Capture and payload rows of every case updated 2026-11-23 (P1.S10 seek format, the piece store's skip stride): every 7th version of a piece's chain is stored as a difference from the version 7 before it (a decode applies at most 12 differences instead of 49), and the capture keeps that anchor's content from the first version stored after it. bm2_work_delta_base_bpf counts those copies (+12 to +25 %, 1.4 to 8.9 KB a frame); an anchor's difference is larger than a frame's, so the full piece is tried a little more often (compress calls and input +4 % on PENTAGON/game and ATM3/idle, -1.6 % on 48K/idle) and the payload moves: bm3_ram_payload_bpf +2.9 % (PENTAGON/game), +0.4 % (PENTAGON/idle), +0.1 % (ATM3/idle), -3.0 % (48K/idle); the device rows (bm2_work_device_blobs_bpf, bm9_device.*) +0.4 to +6 %, bm9_ram_* with them; bm7_file +0.1 to +1.3 %. Sessions of 60 frames have one segment, so the baseline's reuse of unchanged whole versions (which takes payload away in long sessions) does not show here.
